newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Reporters beaten in Albania, equipment broken.
newsitem.headline: Reporters beaten in Albania, equipment broken.

text.p: Albanian police armed with truncheons beat up several reporters covering anti-government rallies on Saturday and smashed or confiscated their equipment.
Police keeping central Tirana's Skanderbeg Square clear of a banned demonstration called by opposition parties pushed away or struck anyone failing to move out of the way quickly enough.
Reporters trying to follow the melee came under particularly fierce attack.
Reuters Television cameraman Leon Cika was struck on the side of the head with a baton as he filmed a demonstrator being hit by a riot policeman.
Three men identifying themselves as special security forces later pushed their way into Reuters Tirana office and demanded the film. They were persuaded to leave.

In the southern town of Fier, Associated Press Television cameraman Spiro Ilo was chased and beaten by regular policemen and plain clothes security forces as he was filming a demonstration against the collapse of pyramid savings schemes.

When an AP photographer, Hektor Pustina, went to complain, he was beaten with bare fists by men in civilian clothes, who left him with a gashed cheek. Eyewitnesses said police officers stood to one side and did not intervene.
Pustina's camera was broken and two of his lenses were stolen.
Reuters reporter Benet Koleka was kicked and beaten with a wooden stick in Fier. Police took his notebook.
In Tirana, Reuters photographer Arben Celi had his camera seized by plainclothes policemen as he was taking pictures of a leader of the opposition Socialist Party being bundled into a police car.
The Interior Ministry had banned the Tirana rally, citing security fears after four days of largely peaceful protests in the southern port of Vlore.
